title: Count Artifacts That Can Be Extracted
summary: Given an n x n grid with artifacts buried in it, and a list of cells to excavate, return the count of artifacts that can be fully uncovered and extracted.
statement: Given an n x n grid with artifacts buried in it, and a list of cells to excavate, return the count of artifacts that can be fully uncovered and extracted. Each artifact is a rectangle defined by its top-left and bottom-right coordinates. No two artifacts overlap, each covers at most 4 cells, and each cell in the dig list is unique.
constraints: Each artifact rectangle is [top,left,bottom,right] with inclusive coordinates.
An artifact counts only when every cell in its rectangle appears in dig.
Artifacts do not overlap, dig cells are unique, and n defines the square grid size.
hints: Dig membership is queried repeatedly, so store coordinates in a set.
For each rectangle, require every row-column coordinate in its inclusive bounds to be excavated.
Build excavated tuples; use all(...) over both inclusive ranges; count successful artifacts.
The Cartesian-product scan visits exactly the cells occupied by an artifact, so all membership tests succeeding is necessary and sufficient.
editorial: The Cartesian-product scan visits exactly the cells occupied by an artifact, so all membership tests succeeding is necessary and sufficient.
